title: Service-credit & Ops-efficiency TCO scenarios — on-prem vs VPC
content:
Purpose:
This is a working spreadsheet-style workbook to model how introducing structured service credits and ops-efficiency guarantees inside Private deployment contracts (on-prem and VPC) changes 3-year TCO and the licensing+support bundle mix.

Quick summary of the idea:
- Problem: customers running on-prem often face large operational headcount costs and unpredictable break/fix incidents. Standard bundles (license + basic support) don’t capture the value we can deliver via runbook automation, managed upgrades, and emergency response credits.
- Hypothesis: offering explicit Service Credits (monetary offsets applied against recurring fees) tied to ops-efficiency SLAs reduces customer upfront objections and increases committed ARR while preserving gross margin if we design the credits to scale with ops savings.

How to use this sheet (notes):
- Top section = inputs/assumptions (editable)
- Middle = scenario generator (conservative / standard / ops-led) with line items for HW, SW (license), support, professional services, finance (leasing), and applied service credits
- Bottom = outputs (3-year NPV-ish TCO, per-token unit economics placeholder, break-even month, sensitivity heatmap inputs)

Key input variables (editable):
- deployment_type: on-prem | vpc
- baseline_hw_capex_per_cluster: $550000 (raw server + networking + storage)
- hw_lifespan_years: 4
- annual_hw_maintenance_pct: 8%
- license_annual_fee_per_cluster: $240000 (base model licensing)
- support_tier_pct_of_license: Basic=10% | Standard=18% | Premium=30%
- managed_ops_fee_monthly: $8000 (if customer buys managed-ops add-on)
- expected_ops_headcount_equivalent_cost_per_year: $220000 per FTE
- ops_headcount_reduction_due_to_automation: scenario dependent (10%/30%/60%)
- service_credit_structure: options: flat-dollar / percent-of-invoice / time-bound credits (we model percent-of-invoice)
- service_credit_rate: scenario dependent (0% / 5% / 12%) applied annually to license+support for year 1-2, stepping down in year 3
- financing_rate_for_hw (if leased): 6% APR over 3y
- incident_rate_per_year: 4 moderate incidents (avg incident ops-hours 80)
- incident_cost_hourly: $150 (ops engagement effective cost)

Scenario definitions (conservative | standard | ops-led):
- Conservative: service_credit_rate = 0%, ops_efficiency = 10% headcount reduction, managed_ops_fee = $0 (customer self-manages). Support tier = Standard (18%).
- Standard: service_credit_rate = 5% year1, 3% year2, 1% year3; ops_efficiency = 30% headcount reduction from automation & runbooks; managed_ops_fee = $6000/mo; Support tier = Standard (18%).
- Ops-led: service_credit_rate = 12% y1, 8% y2, 4% y3; ops_efficiency = 60% headcount reduction; managed_ops_fee = $12000/mo (higher value, includes runbook automation managed), Support tier = Premium (30%).

Core formulas (plain language):
- HW_total_3yr_cost = HW_capex + (ownership maintenance * 3) OR financed(lease) payments
- SW_total_3yr_cost = license_annual_fee * 3 (with maybe per-year step ups)
- Support_total_3yr_cost = license_annual_fee * support_tier_pct * 3
- Ops_cost_3yr = FTE_eq_cost * baseline_headcount * (1 - ops_efficiency) * 3 + incident_costs_offset_by_automation
- Managed_ops_fees_3yr = managed_ops_fee_monthly * 12 * 3 (if the customer buys it)
- Service_credits_total_3yr = sum(yearly(service_credit_rate_year_n * (license+support)))
- Net_TCO_3yr = HW_total_3yr + SW_total_3yr + Support_total_3yr + Ops_cost_3yr + Managed_ops_fees_3yr + PS_one_time - Service_credits_total_3yr

Example numbers (single-cluster illustrative):
- Baseline (Conservative, on-prem):
  - HW capex: $550,000
  - SW (3yr): $720,000
  - Support (3yr @18%): $129,600
  - Ops (3yr, 2 FTE baseline, 10% reduction): = 2 * $220,000 * (1 - 0.10) * 3 = $1,188,000
  - Managed ops fees: $0
  - Service credits: $0
  - Net_TCO_3yr = $550,000 + $720,000 + $129,600 + $1,188,000 = $2,587,600

- Standard (VPC, standard bundle + managed ops):
  - HW: $0 (cloud) but include provider committed capacity fee equivalent $150,000/yr -> 3yr = $450,000
  - SW (3yr license): $720,000
  - Support (3yr @18%): $129,600
  - Ops (3yr baseline 2 FTE, 30% reduction): = 2 * $220,000 * (1 - 0.30) * 3 = $924,000
  - Managed ops fees (3yr): $6,000 * 12 * 3 = $216,000
  - Service credits (5% first year etc): approx $54,000 total across 3yrs
  - Net_TCO_3yr ≈ $450,000 + $720,000 + $129,600 + $924,000 + $216,000 - $54,000 = $2,385,600

- Ops-led (On-prem + premium support + managed ops):
  - HW capex: $550,000 (same)
  - SW (3yr): $720,000
  - Support (3yr @30%): $216,000
  - Ops (3yr baseline 2 FTE, 60% reduction): = 2 * 220k * (1 - 0.60) * 3 = $528,000
  - Managed ops fees (3yr): $12,000 * 12 * 3 = $432,000
  - Service credits (12%/8%/4%): approx $150,000 across 3yrs
  - Net_TCO_3yr ≈ $550,000 + $720,000 + $216,000 + $528,000 + $432,000 - $150,000 = $2,296,000

Observation from example rows:
- Ops-led pack reduces net TCO compared to Conservative even though managed fees and premium support are higher — because ops headcount delta dominates.
- VPC standard shows competitive TCO vs on-prem conservative because customer avoids HW capex and may accept provider committed capacity fees.
- Service credits materially improve buyer psychology: they reduce initial perceived risk and can be structured to be redeemable only when ops SLAs aren't met, which caps Redwood exposure.

Sensitivity tests to add (suggested tab):
- Vary ops_efficiency from 0% to 80% in 10% steps; observe break-even support tier and managed fee required to keep Net_TCO <= conservative baseline.
- Vary service_credit_rate from 0% to 15% and test margin impact (gross margin delta) assuming Redwood covers credits from services margin bucket.
- Incident frequency sensitivity: double/halve incident_rate_per_year and recompute onsite engagement costs.
- Lease vs buy for HW: test 0% upfront (fully financed) vs full-capex impacts on customer cashflow break-even.

Commercial structuring ideas (playbook bullets):
- Offer a 3-tier Service Credit ladder: 12% y1 / 8% y2 / 4% y3 tied to ops-efficiency milestones (measured by incident hours and MTTR reductions). Credits only payable if ops-efficiency targets not achieved (reduces Redwood payout likelihood).
- Bundle managed-ops credits: discount first 6 months of managed-ops fee if customer buys Premium support + 24m commit; use that to defray PS onboarding costs.
- Customer success KPI: define a simple operational scorecard (incident hours, upgrade success rate, patch latency) — credits are escrowed internally and only released against failed KPIs.
- Sales motion: for hybrid accounts, propose a blended TCO view that shows a 12-24 month runway to ops break-even when opting into Redwood-managed automation.

Open questions / data we need to finalize model:
- True baseline ops FTE equivalents per customer cluster (survey needed across 12 pilot customers)
- Typical financed HW lease terms we can offer via partners (we currently assume 3yr at 6% APR; get legal/finance to validate)
- Real incident cost numbers (we have anecdotal logs; need SRE/PS to provide averages)
- Legal input: acceptable framing of Service Credits in contract (limit liability, caps per year, redemption rules)

Action items:
- [Aisha] run a short survey with four pilot on-prem customers to capture FTE, incident rates, and willingness to trade credits for managed ops (due 2026-03-17)
- [Marco] add a sensitivity tab for ops_efficiency and service_credit_rate with automated charts (due 2026-03-12)
- [Jasmine] validate support tier pricing and margin impact with finance (due 2026-03-15)
- [Tom] draft sample contract language for the Service Credit escrow and payout triggers (legal review required)

Notes to reviewer:
- This is intentionally a working sheet. Numbers are illustrative and rounded. Use the sensitivity tab to test real customer data once we have it.
- If we proceed, propose a 3-customer pilot to validate the operational measurement approach and calibrate credit bands.

Appendix (quick reference table):
- Headcount assumptions per cluster: baseline = 2 FTE (platform ops) per cluster; heavy = 4 FTE; light = 1 FTE
- PS onboarding: one-time professional services assumed $120k per cluster (on-prem install, integration, training)
- Upgrade window cost (manual): 40 ops-hours per major upgrade; automated upgrade: 6 ops-hours
- Credit cap: suggest cap = min(annual service credits, 20% of annual recurring fees) to limit Redwood exposure

End of doc — iterative draft for internal review.
